payload.title: What could go wrong? — a life narrowed by correlated judgments
payload.description: Ryan's story premise: an ordinary detail in a man's biography leads decision models to infer an identity incorrectly and apply a stereotype. Separate institutions can repeat the mistake through shared models or learned associations; repeated exclusion damages his circumstances and becomes fresh evidence against him. He experiences narrowing options without discovering the cause. Develop a documented case and counterfactual evidence; keep the speculative chain explicit until established. Related to The End of the Rave: inferred identity acquires authority over access.
